newsitem.title: INDIA: India sugar extends gains on festival buying.
newsitem.headline: India sugar extends gains on festival buying.

text.p: Sugar prices extended gains on the local market on Thursday as increased consumer buying for approaching festivals dragged prices upward, with supplies at low ebb, dealers said.
In the ready delivery sugar S-30 rose by 8 rupees at 1,480/1,508 rupees per quintal while sugar M-30 looked up by five rupees at 1,500/1,540 rupees per quintal.
"Offerings by millers remained low due to lower than required free sale quota for the current month," a broker said.
The August free sale quota is 750,000 tonnes, the same as for July. The June quota was 800,000 tonne.
"Free sale quota of 750,000 tonnes for August is not sufficient looking at the approaching Hindu festivals," he said.
"Unless government releases extra quota, sugar prices will remain firm in the coming days on the back of seasonal buying," he added.

Trading in sugar mill delivery resumed after a lapse of a few days and S-30 was quoted at 1,415/1,425 rupees per quintal and M-30 at 1,435/1,455 rupees per quintal. Sugar mill delivery had been unquoted over the last four days as local millers had sold out the entire free sale quota allotted to them for July.
Overall market sentiment was firm at the close of the session.
